request.spec:
The consolidated figures gain, per grade on any sheet of the tree, the due-totals of the people on
that grade (retired people left out) added up over the tree, and per status the count of claims in
that status over the tree.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The consolidated figures gain, per grade on any sheet of the tree, the due-totals of the people on
that grade (retired people left out) added up over the tree, and per status the count of claims in
that status over the tree.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The consolidated figures now show a due-total for each grade and a claim count for each status, added up over the sheet and every sheet below it. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

The whole change is in `src/main/frontend/features/consolidated/ConsolidatedFigures.tsx`. That component already walked the sheet tree to add up people, due and overdue. I added two more running totals to that walk:

- **Grade due-totals** (`consolidated-grade-{A,B,C}-due-total`): for each sheet, I take its people on each grade today, leave out retired people, skip any "n/a" due-totals, and add the sheet's figure to the tree total. This is the same calculation the sheet's own summary panel uses, so the numbers match it.
- **Status counts** (`consolidated-status-{DRAFT,OPEN,PENDING,SETTLED,VOID,REVIEW}-count`): each sheet's count of claims in that status, added up over the tree.

The overall consolidated due-total leaves out each sheet's single highest and lowest person when the sheet has three or more people. The new per-grade figures include everyone, as the summary panel does. So on sheets with three or more people, the grade figures may not add up to the overall due-total.

No server or stored-data changes were needed, because every figure is already worked out on the front end from data each sheet loads.
